output.reasoning: The listing disclosed minor sleeve scuffs and the photos show them, so that part of the complaint is not a seller fault. The buyer also reports a worn collar, which was not mentioned in the listing or photographed, so the buyer has a partly valid point. Offering a partial refund of 60 CAD settles the undisclosed collar wear quickly without refunding the full amount for a pre-owned item that was described as having scuffs.

evidenceUsed.point: The listing described the jacket as pre-owned in good condition with minor scuffs on the sleeves and referred buyers to photos.
The seller's statement says the listing photos show the sleeve scuffs and the collar was not photographed.
The buyer says there are scuffs on both sleeves and a worn collar.
The buyer's PayPal message says the jacket has visible scratches and wear and is not as described.
Canada Post tracking shows the order was delivered on 2026-10-20 with no signature on delivery.

evidenceGaps: Photos or notes showing the collar condition at the time of sale.
Whether the buyer wore the jacket, which affects the listing's 14-day unworn return policy.
Any written description or inspection notes beyond the listing text, such as a condition checklist.

alternatives.whyNot: The collar wear is not documented in the listing or photos, so the seller lacks specific evidence to defend the full claim.
The sleeve scuffs were disclosed in the listing and photos, so a full refund would overpay for the part the seller did disclose.

output.draftNote: Regarding this dispute, the listing described this pre-owned leather jacket as good condition with minor sleeve scuffs and referred to photos showing them. The buyer has raised a concern about a worn collar, which was not shown in the listing photos. To resolve this, we are offering a partial refund of 60 CAD. We are glad to discuss this further.
nextSteps: Review the offer of 60 CAD against the collar concern and the listing text before submitting.
Submit the offer through PayPal with a short note explaining the basis for the amount.
Keep the listing, photos, and Canada Post tracking record on file in case the buyer declines the offer.
Check whether the buyer accepts the offer before the dispute window closes.
